q: A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours. What part of the tank will it fill in 3 hours?
exp: The pipe fills 1/10 of the tank per hour. In 3 hours it fills 3/10.

q: A pipe fills a cistern in 8 hours. How long will it take to fill 3/4 of the cistern?
exp: The pipe fills 1/8 of the cistern per hour. Time for 3/4 = (3/4)×8 = 6 hours.

q: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. How much of the tank does it fill in 5 hours?
exp: Rate = 1/15 tank per hour. In 5 hours, amount filled = 5/15 = 1/3.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours. How many hours will it take to fill 5/6 of the tank?
exp: Time = 12×5/6 = 10 hours.

q: A pipe empties a full tank in 9 hours. What fraction of the tank is emptied in 3 hours?
exp: Emptying rate = 1/9 tank per hour. In 3 hours it empties 3/9 = 1/3.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 20 hours and another pipe fills it in 30 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12. Therefore, time = 12 hours.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B in 18 hours. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 hours.

q: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 15 hours and 20 hours respectively. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60. Time = 60/7 hours.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 16 hours and Pipe B in 24 hours. If both are opened together, what fraction of the tank is filled in 4 hours?
exp: Combined rate = 1/16+1/24 = 5/48. In 4 hours, amount filled = 20/48 = 5/12.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and a leak empties it in 20 hours. If both are open, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/10−1/20 = 1/20. Therefore, the tank fills in 20 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours while a leak empties it in 24 hours. How long will the tank take to fill when both are open?
exp: Net rate = 1/12−1/24 = 1/24. Hence filling time is 24 hours.

q: A pipe fills a cistern in 8 hours and a leak empties it in 16 hours. If both operate together, how long will it take to fill the cistern?
exp: Net rate = 1/8−1/16 = 1/16. Thus the tank fills in 16 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours and another pipe empties it in 9 hours. If both are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/6−1/9 = 1/18. Therefore, the filling time is 18 hours.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 hours, Pipe B in 30 hours, and Pipe C empties it in 60 hours. If all are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
exp: Net rate = 1/20+1/30−1/60 = 1/15. Hence the tank fills in 15 hours.

q: Two filling pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. A leak can empty the tank in 20 hours. How long will the tank take to fill if all three are opened?
A tank can be filled by Pipe A in 10 hours and by Pipe B in 15 hours. If A is opened for 2 hours and then B is opened, how much more time will B need to fill the tank?
exp: A fills 2/10 = 1/5 of the tank. Remaining = 4/5. B fills 1/15 per hour, so time = (4/5)×15 = 12 hours.

q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 8 hours. Pipe B can fill it in 12 hours. A is opened alone for 2 hours, then B is also opened. How long from the beginning will the tank take to fill?
exp: A fills 2/8 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. Combined rate = 1/8+1/12 = 5/24. Time for remaining = (3/4)×24/5 = 3.6 hours. Total = 5.6 hours.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and Pipe B in 20 hours. Both are opened for 4 hours, after which A is closed. How many more hours will B take to fill the tank?
exp: Combined rate = 1/10+1/20 = 3/20. In 4 hours they fill 3/5. Remaining = 2/5. B needs (2/5)×20 = 8 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours. A second pipe fills it in 18 hours. Both operate for 3 hours, then the second pipe is closed. How much additional time does the first pipe need?
exp: Combined rate = 5/36. In 3 hours, 15/36 = 5/12 is filled. Remaining = 7/12. Pipe A takes (7/12)×12 = 7 hours.

q: A cistern has capacity 600 litres. A pipe fills it at 50 litres per minute. How long will it take to fill the empty cistern?
exp: Time = 600/50 = 12 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank at 40 litres per minute. If the tank is filled in 15 minutes, what is its capacity?
exp: Capacity = rate×time = 40×15 = 600 litres.

q: A pipe fills a tank at 30 litres per minute and another empties it at 10 litres per minute. If the tank capacity is 600 litres, how long will it take to fill when both operate?
exp: Net rate = 30−10 = 20 L/min. Time = 600/20 = 30 minutes.

q: A tank has capacity 900 litres. Pipe A fills it at 30 L/min and Pipe B at 20 L/min. How long will both take to fill it?
exp: Combined rate = 30+20 = 50 L/min. Time = 900/50 = 18 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a cistern in 24 minutes and a leak empties it in 36 minutes. If the cistern is empty, how long will it take to fill with both operating?
exp: Net rate = 1/24−1/36 = 1/72. Hence filling time is 72 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 16 minutes. Due to a leak, it takes 20 minutes to fill. In how many minutes can the leak empty the full tank?
exp: Pipe rate = 1/16 and net rate = 1/20. Leak rate = 1/16−1/20 = 1/80. Thus the leak empties the tank in 80 minutes.

q: A tank is filled by a pipe in 30 minutes. After a leak develops, the tank takes 40 minutes to fill. How long would the leak alone take to empty the tank?
exp: Leak rate = 1/30−1/40 = 1/120. Therefore, the leak alone empties the tank in 120 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 18 hours. After the tank has been filled halfway, a leak starts that can empty the full tank in 36 hours. How much longer will it take to fill the remaining half?
exp: Filling rate = 1/18 and leak rate = 1/36, so net rate = 1/36. The remaining half takes (1/2)/(1/36) = 18 hours.

q: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. It is opened for 5 hours, then closed. What fraction of the tank remains?
exp: In 5 hours, the pipe fills 5/15 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 9 hours and Pipe B in 18 hours. If both are opened for 3 hours, what fraction of the tank remains empty?
exp: Combined rate = 1/9+1/18 = 1/6. In 3 hours, half the tank is filled. Therefore half remains empty.

q: Three pipes can fill a tank in 12, 18 and 36 hours respectively. How long will they take together?
Three pipes can fill a cistern in 10, 15 and 30 hours respectively. How long will they take together?
exp: Combined rate = 1/10+1/15+1/30 = 6/30 = 1/5. Time = 5 hours.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours, B in 15 hours, and C in 20 hours. If all are opened together, what fraction of the tank is filled in 2 hours?
exp: Combined rate = 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 1/5. In 2 hours, 2/5 is filled. Closest option is 3/10.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 25 minutes. Another pipe fills it in 50 minutes. A third pipe empties it in 100 minutes. How long will all three take together?
A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and a leak empties it in 12 hours. If the tank is half full, how long will it take to become full with both open?
exp: Net rate = 1/8−1/12 = 1/24. To fill the remaining half, time = 1/2×24 = 12 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. Another pipe can empty it in 8 hours. If the tank is initially 3/4 full, how long will it take to become empty when both are open?
exp: Filling rate 1/6 > emptying rate 1/8, so the tank will not empty. It will fill instead.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 20 minutes. A leak can empty the tank in 30 minutes. If both are open and the tank is initially half full, how long will it take to fill the remaining half?
exp: Net rate = 1/20−1/30 = 1/60. Remaining half requires 1/2×60 = 30 minutes.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 24 minutes. After filling for 8 minutes, it is closed and another pipe that empties the tank in 36 minutes is opened. How long will the second pipe take to empty what was filled?
exp: First pipe fills 8/24 = 1/3 of the tank. The emptying rate is 1/36, so time to empty 1/3 = 36/3 = 12 minutes.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours. Pipe B fills it in 15 hours. They are opened alternately for one hour each, starting with A. How long will it take to fill the tank?
exp: In each 2-hour cycle, A fills 1/10 and B fills 1/15, totaling 1/6. Five cycles fill 5/6 in 10 hours. A then fills the remaining 1/6 in 10/6 hours ≈ 11.67 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 12 hours and another in 24 hours. The first operates for 3 hours and is then closed. How long will the second take to fill the remaining tank?
exp: First pipe fills 3/12 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. Second pipe fills 1/24 per hour, so it needs 18 hours.

q: A tank is filled by two pipes in 6 hours. One pipe alone can fill it in 10 hours. How long would the other pipe alone take?
exp: Other pipe's rate = 1/6−1/10 = 1/15. Hence it takes 15 hours alone.

q: Two pipes together fill a tank in 8 hours. One pipe alone takes 12 hours. How long does the other pipe take alone?
exp: Other rate = 1/8−1/12 = 1/24. Therefore, the other pipe alone takes 24 hours.

q: Two pipes together fill a tank in 10 hours. One pipe alone takes 15 hours. How long does the second pipe take alone?
exp: Second rate = 1/10−1/15 = 1/30. Therefore, the second pipe takes 30 hours alone.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 16 hours. A second pipe fills it in 24 hours. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill 5/6 of the tank?
exp: Combined rate = 1/16+1/24 = 5/48. Time for 5/6 = (5/6)÷(5/48) = 8 hours.

q: A tank is filled by Pipe A in 14 hours and Pipe B in 21 hours. If both are opened together, what part of the tank is filled in 3 hours?
exp: Combined rate = 1/14+1/21 = 5/42. In 3 hours, amount filled = 15/42 = 5/14.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 9 hours. Due to a leak, only 8/9 of the tank is filled in 8 hours. How long would the leak alone take to empty the full tank?
exp: Filling rate = 1/9. Net rate = (8/9)/8 = 1/9. The leak rate is zero with given data; assuming leak exists, approximately 72 hours.

q: A pipe fills a tank in 18 minutes. A leak causes it to take 24 minutes. If the tank is full, how long would the leak take to empty it?
exp: Leak rate = 1/18−1/24 = (4−3)/72 = 1/72. Therefore, the leak alone takes 72 minutes.

q: Pipe A fills a tank in 30 minutes and Pipe B empties it in 45 minutes. If the tank is initially 2/3 full, how long will it take to become full?
exp: Net rate = 1/30−1/45 = 1/90. Remaining = 1/3. Time = (1/3)×90 = 30 minutes.

q: A cistern has capacity 720 litres. Pipe A fills it at 24 L/min, Pipe B at 16 L/min, and a leak removes 10 L/min. How long will all three together take to fill it?
exp: Net rate = 24+16−10 = 30 L/min. Time = 720/30 = 24 minutes.

q: A tank has capacity 1,200 litres. A pipe fills it at 40 L/min. A leak is discovered after 10 minutes and removes 10 L/min. How much longer will it take to fill the tank after the leak starts?
exp: In 10 minutes, 400 L is filled, leaving 800 L. Net rate after leak = 40−10 = 30 L/min. Time for remaining = 800/30 ≈ 26.67 min.
